answer_1.quote: We task the two best-performing open-weight and closed-source models, Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and GPT-4o, with answering three different types of prompts aimed at: i) definition generation, ii) free-form explanation, iii) example generation
datasets: Maru et al. 2022 WSD test set
answer_1.outputs: definitions, explanations, and example sentences for words in context

answer_4.quote: we request an expert annotator with strong background in computational lexical semantics to tag the outputs generated by the models in the three tasks
answer_4.guideline: For the dictionary-style definition generation task we ask the annotator to tag the definitions provided by the two LLMs in comparison with the WordNet definitions as selected in the gold standard dataset. For each item, the annotator has four options: equally correct, better than gold, worse than gold, wrong. In the free explanation task the annotator has to evaluate the quality of the unconstrained explanation produced by the models for the target word in context. The evaluation options include good, bad and borderline. In the example generation task the annotator has to assess the ability of the LLMs to generate three distinct sentences that use the target word in the same sense as in the sentence under examination. In this case four options could be selected: yes (all three sentences are accurate), yes but same pattern, no (at least one sentence is clearly incorrect), and borderline
